$comment: Hints that come back with a command's result when its output matches. Edit freely: each entry needs output (a regular expression, case-insensitive, matched against stdout and stderr) and hint (what the model is told, as [hint: ...]). Optional: tools (which tools it applies to: run, sudo, run_playbook; default all three) and command (a regular expression the command must match too). Checked by tests/hints_test.ts.

hints.output: a terminal is required|a password is required|no tty present|askpass
hints.hint: sudo on the other machine wanted a password, which cannot be typed through ssh inside run. Use sudo -n there to fail fast, or do it machine by machine with the ssh tool and then the sudo tool (which handle the password).

hints.output: a terminal is required|a password is required|no tty present|askpass
hints.hint: sudo in the playbook wanted a password, which a playbook cannot type. Use sudo -n with a NOPASSWD rule for that command, or take the root step out and do it with the sudo tool.

hints.output: permission denied while trying to connect to the docker
hints.hint: docker refused this login. Check `getent group docker` and `id -nG`: if the user is in the group but this login is not, the login predates it: ssh_exit and ssh again (a fresh login), or run it as sg docker -c '<command>'. If they are not in it, adding them (usermod -aG docker <user>, with the sudo tool) is the user's call.

hints.output: address already in use|bind\(\) to .* failed|port is already allocated
hints.hint: the port is taken. See what holds it (ss -ltnp or lsof -i :<port>) before stopping anything; if it is one of the user's servers, ask first, or pick the free port listed under Where you are.
the disk is full. Look at what is using it (df -h, du -sh on the models folder and caches) and ask the user what may go; remove_downloads cleans up ai-bootstrap's own model downloads.

hints.output: CUDA out of memory|cudaMalloc failed|out of memory allocating|failed to allocate .* (on device|buffer)
hints.hint: the GPU ran out of memory. Check what else holds it (nvidia-smi), then use a smaller quantization, a shorter context, fewer layers on the GPU, or a lower --gpu-memory-utilization.
